proposals.title: CanonicalEncoder with trusted-intrinsic isolation (ADR-009 third attempt)
proposals.why_now: TASK-0004 has been rejected twice by the reviewer. Both rejections cite the same two defects: (1) container traversal invokes user-controllable code — Proxy traps on ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, getPrototypeOf, overridden Set Symbol.iterator, and array index accessors — and (2) encoding behavior depends on mutable global built-ins (Number.isNaN, Number.isInteger, Object.getPrototypeOf, Reflect.ownKeys, Set, Uint8Array) that callers can replace after module import. ADR-009 §9 already promises these paths are isolated but the implementation does not honour that promise. The encoder is the explicit FASE-1 prerequisite for StateHash. Nothing downstream of StateHash can proceed until this is accepted.

proposals.title: Specify ADR-002 and implement positional RNG in packages/core
proposals.why_now: The price generator (trendLayer, idiosyncraticNoise, marketFactor, macroEvent slots) requires rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) -> uint64. ADR-002 marks the hash function as DEFINIR with the constraint that it be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR and must not be the language's native hash. This work is independent of the CanonicalEncoder and can proceed in parallel. Without it, INV-02 (direct price query equals tick-by-tick result) cannot be tested and the two-asset price generator required by FASE-1 cannot be built.

proposals.title: Implement branded numeric domain types in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-003 requires Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick as nominal branded types with constructor validators that reject non-integers and out-of-range values. These types are the foundation for ledger, order, and domain logic. Implementing them now establishes the compile-time and runtime barriers that prevent float usage and cross-type arithmetic errors before any domain code is written. They depend on nothing else in packages/core (not on the encoder, not on the RNG) and can proceed immediately.

proposals.title: Implement ADR-004 and division helpers in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-004 requires that every division declare an explicit rounding mode and that the residue be lanced to a rounding-residue account. The technical mechanism for enforcing this (lint rule or type-level wrapper) is a DEFINIR item. Implementing the division helpers alongside an ADR resolving this DEFINIR item prevents silent precision loss in the ledger before any economic computation is written. It can proceed once branded types (IDEA-003) are accepted since helpers operate on Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate.

proposals.title: Electron main-process security scaffold satisfying INV-29
proposals.why_now: INV-29 requires contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, and sandbox:true in all execution modes including development. FASE-1 acceptance explicitly includes INV-29 green and requires the simulation to run in a dedicated worker. The current apps/desktop/main/src/index.ts is an empty stub. Implementing the minimum BrowserWindow creation with enforced security options and preload channel allowlist establishes the Electron security baseline before any renderer or worker code is added, preventing the cost of retrofitting security constraints onto a permissive baseline later.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo bootstrap is complete: all 16 mandated workspace packages exist as typed stubs, strict TypeScript and ESLint determinism lint are active and passing, and the dependency-boundary checker is enforcing the §14.5 directed graph. No production logic has been committed to any package. TASK-0004 (ADR-009 + CanonicalEncoder) has been attempted twice and rejected both times for the same two implementation defects: container traversal invokes user-controllable Proxy traps and overridden iterators, and encoding behavior reads mutable global built-ins that callers can replace after module import. No other FASE-1 deliverable has been attempted. The docs/decisions directory contains no ADRs.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009) is the explicit prerequisite stated in the FASE-1 acceptance criteria ('ADR-009 escrito e o encoder implementado antes de qualquer hash de estado existir'). After two failed attempts the implementation defects are precisely identified: trusted-intrinsic capture and Proxy-safe container traversal. Until a passing implementation is accepted, StateHash cannot be produced, the replay CLI cannot compare run outputs, and INV-01, INV-22, and all hash-dependent invariants cannot be tested.

warnings: TASK-0004 has been attempted and rejected twice with identical root causes in both reviews. The required changes are documented precisely in TASK-0004-review-02 findings REVIEW-001 and REVIEW-002. A third attempt that does not address both findings in ADR-009 and in implementation will repeat the same outcome. The acceptance criteria for IDEA-001 make both fixes explicit.

ADR-002 marks the hash function as DEFINIR. The implementation is free to choose SplitMix64 over FNV-1a (the spec's own recommendation) but the choice must be specified bit-by-bit in the ADR before any golden vectors are committed. Changing the hash function after golden vectors are locked requires a breaking encodingVersion bump.

ADR-004 is a DEFINIR item for the technical enforcement mechanism of explicit rounding modes. Until the ADR resolves whether enforcement is a lint rule or a type-level wrapper, division helpers cannot claim full compliance. IDEA-004 must resolve this DEFINIR item in its ADR before committing enforcement code.
